content: Two blocks ( and ) with respectively masses 2 kg and 1.5 kg are joined by a massless thread. These blocks are mounted on a frictionless pully which is fixed on the edge of a cube , as shown in the figure below. Block is positioned on the top surface which has no friction and block is in contact with side-surface, having coefficient friction . The cube ( ) moves towards the right with acceleration of , where is gravitational acceleration. During this movement the block and remain stationary. The value of is (take )
explanation:
Since the cube is accelerating at to the right, when analysing the blocks from the cube's non-inertial frame, we must apply a pseudo-force ( ) on both blocks in the opposite direction to the acceleration of block S.

For block P (Mass )

Along horizontal the tension (T) in the thread pulls it to the right. The pseudo-force ( ) pulls it to the left. Along vertical direction gravity ( ) acts downward and normal force ( ) from the top surface acts upward. Since the block is stationary relative to the cube :

For block Q (Mass )

Along horizontal direction the cube pushes against the block with a normal force to the right. The pseudoforce acts to the left.

Along vertical direction, gravity ( ) acts downward.

Tension (T) in the thread acts upward, [as the string is massless and inextensible]

Friction (f) acts upward to prevent the block from falling.

For equilibrium in the vertical direction:
